question: State Ampere’s circuital law. Using this law, derive the expression for the magnetic field at a distance $r$ from a long straight conductor carrying current $I$. Hence calculate the magnetic field at a distance $8.0\text{ cm}$ from a long straight wire carrying current $15\text{ A}$. Take $\mu_0=4\pi\times10^{-7}\text{ T m A}^{-1}$.

options.D: Ampere’s law is $\oint\vec B\cdot d\vec l=\mu_0I$. Symmetry gives $B(2\pi r)=\mu_0I$, so $B=\dfrac{\mu_0I}{2\pi r}=\dfrac{(4\pi\times10^{-7})(15)}{2\pi(0.08)}=3.75\times10^{-5}\,\text{T}$.
